title: Dryer Vent Cleaning in Collingwood: Warning Signs and Safe Checks

html:
Longer drying times, unusual heat, weak airflow at the outside flap or lint around the dryer are good reasons to inspect the vent. Stop using the appliance if you smell burning, see smoke or sparking, or suspect a gas or electrical fault. Those situations need the appropriate qualified professional rather than routine vent cleaning.

A dryer vent can also be harder to monitor in a cottage or vacation property. The route may be long, the exterior hood may be blocked by snow or foliage, or the property may sit unused long enough for debris or pests to affect the termination.

Why dryer vent maintenance matters

The lint screen does not replace maintenance of the exhaust system. Warm, moist air and lint must travel through the duct and discharge outdoors. Restricted airflow can make drying take longer and can contribute to lint buildup and overheating.

Natural Resources Canada advises keeping the outside exhaust vent clean and warns that lint buildup in the exhaust duct and outside vent is a potential fire hazard. Its guidance recommends inspecting and cleaning the duct and vent at least annually, while following the dryer's owner manual.

NFPA recommends cleaning the lint filter before or after each load, checking that the exhaust pipe is not restricted and confirming that the outdoor flap opens while the dryer is operating.

Five signs the vent needs attention

1. Loads take longer to dry

A load that used to dry in one cycle but now needs another deserves attention. Restricted airflow is one possible cause, but an overloaded drum, very wet clothing, a full lint screen or an appliance fault can produce the same symptom.

2. The dryer or laundry room feels unusually hot

Dryers produce heat, but excessive heat around the appliance or clothing that feels unusually hot is not something to ignore. Turn the dryer off if the heat is accompanied by a burning smell, smoke or other abnormal behaviour.

3. The exterior flap barely opens

From a safe position at ground level, check the outside hood while the dryer is running. The flap should open as air leaves the system. Weak movement may point to lint, a blocked hood, a crushed or separated connection, or a vent route that needs assessment.

4. You notice musty odours or excess moisture

Dryer exhaust should not discharge into a basement, crawlspace, attic or enclosed room. Health Canada says clothes dryers should vent outdoors through a wall or roof to help prevent excess moisture and mould growth.

5. Lint appears around the dryer or exterior hood

Lint in unusual places can indicate a loose connection, damaged duct, blocked hood or poor exhaust flow. Do not rely on repeatedly brushing away visible lint without finding the underlying issue.

Checks homeowners can make safely

  • Clean the lint screen before or after every load.
  • From ground level, check that the exterior hood is visible and free of snow, leaves, lint and nesting material. Health Canada also recommends routinely inspecting the outside exhaust vent.
  • Make sure the dryer has not been pushed tightly against the wall and crushed the connection.
  • Look for an obvious kink, gap or detached section without dismantling unfamiliar connections while the dryer is operating.
  • Follow the manufacturer's instructions for access, cleaning and replacement parts.

Do not climb onto a roof or enter a crawlspace just to inspect the vent. If the hood is high, the route is enclosed or access equipment may be needed, mention that when requesting an estimate.

Turn off the dryer and arrange appropriate help if there is smoke, a burning odour, sparking, repeated overheating or a suspected gas or electrical problem. A gas dryer or electrical fault may require an appliance technician, gas professional or electrician.

Why cottage properties and long runs need planning

A laundry room far from an exterior wall may have a longer or more complicated duct route. More bends and concealed sections can make inspection and cleaning less straightforward. Seasonal properties also need a practical plan for checking the outside termination after periods of vacancy.

Before contacting a service provider, gather:

  • the dryer's location and approximate route to the exterior;
  • whether the dryer is electric or gas;
  • the symptoms and when they began;
  • ground-level photos of the dryer connection and exterior hood, if safely accessible; and
  • any access limits caused by a crawlspace, finished ceiling, roof outlet or remote property.

What to clarify in a dryer vent cleaning quote

The scope depends on the layout and condition of the system. Ask whether the estimate covers:

  • inspection of the dryer connection and visible route;
  • cleaning of the accessible duct and exterior hood;
  • checking the exterior flap and airflow after cleaning;
  • reconnecting or securing a loose section; and
  • minor repairs or replacement of a damaged hood or duct section.

Cleaning may not solve a faulty heating element, motor, thermostat, control board, seal or other appliance problem. Changes to a vent route should also be checked against the manufacturer's instructions and applicable building requirements.

Ontario's Building Code states that exhaust ducts connected to laundry-drying equipment must discharge directly outdoors, be independent of other exhaust ducts, be designed so the entire duct can be cleaned and be made of smooth corrosion-resistant material. The current provisions are set out in the 2024 Ontario Building Code Compendium. For a new installation or significant alteration, confirm the project requirements with the municipality and the appliance manufacturer.
